bills.title: Bond levy increase period
bills.description: Extending the period for which a bond levy may be increased.

bills.title: Basic education funding
bills.description: Funding fully the state's program of basic education by providing equitable education opportunities through reform of state and local education contributions.

bills.title: Low-income housing/REET
bills.description: Providing a real estate excise tax exemption for certain transfers of low-income housing.

bills.title: Accountable communities
bills.description: Providing a business and occupation tax exemption for accountable communities of health.

bills.title: Schools/excess levies
bills.description: Delaying implementation of revisions to the school levy lid. (REVISED FOR ENGROSSED: Changing provisions relating to school district excess levies. )

bills.title: Trans. benefit tax increase
bills.description: Authorizing certain public transportation benefit areas to impose a sales and use tax increase approved by voters.

bills.title: Renewable energy promotion
bills.description: Promoting a sustainable, local renewable energy industry through modifying renewable energy system tax incentives and providing guidance for renewable energy system component recycling.

bills.title: Electrolytic processing tax
bills.description: Extending the expiration date of the public utility tax exemption for certain electrolytic processing businesses.

bills.title: Common school funding
bills.description: Concerning funding for the support of common schools. (REVISED FOR ENGROSSED: Providing property tax relief by reducing calendar year 2019 state property taxes and redirecting revenue to the education legacy trust account for fiscal year 2019 )

notes: EHB 2242, the 2017 McCleary school funding law, is counted as a tax increase. It raised the state school property tax from 2018 and capped local school levies from 2019; no state revenue estimate was published, but the state increase came first and was larger.

SSB 5977, the 2017 tax preference bill, is counted as a tax cut without a state revenue estimate (none was published for it). The governor vetoed its manufacturing B&O rate cut and signed the rest, which extends tax breaks.

Three bills are counted as tax increases without a state revenue estimate because they raise local taxing limits or authority: ESB 5023 (kept school levy limits from dropping for 2018), SHB 1344 (lets Thurston County use a levy lid lift for bond payments for up to 25 years) and ESB 5288 (lets Pierce Transit ask voters for 0.3% more sales tax).
